newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli who cursed Rabin gets 4-month jail term.
newsitem.headline: Israeli who cursed Rabin gets 4-month jail term.

text.p: An Israeli court ordered a man be sent to prison for four months on Sunday for putting a curse on Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin a month before the Israeli leader was assassinated.

Court spokesman Moshe Gorali said the court ordered the jail term for Avigdor Eskin along with a year's suspended sentence on charges he violated a part of the Prevention of Terrorism Act which bars encouragement of violence.

According to local news reports at the time, Eskin stood outside Rabin's house on the eve of the Jewish high holy day of Yom Kippur in 1995 and cursed Rabin with the ancient curse of "pulsa denura" -- Aramaic for "lashes of fire".

The curse Eskin put on Rabin read in part: "And on him, Yitzhak, son of Rosa, known as Rabin, we have permission...to demand from angels of destruction that they take a sword to this wicked man...to kill him...for handing over the Land of Israel to our enemies."
He said the curse generally worked within 30 days.

Roughly one month later, on November 4, right-wing Jewish law student Yigal Amir gunned down Rabin after a peace rally in Tel Aviv. Amir said he hoped to stop the prime minister from handing over land to Palestinians in peace deals.

Israeli reporters quoted Eskin when he left the courtroom on Sunday as saying he would not challenge the sentence so long as he could spend the four months in the same cell as Amir, who is being held in solitary confinement.
Rabin was the first Israeli prime minister to be assassinated.
